legend: Templates for this problem are available here.
Alice is standing at position 1$$$1$$$ of a straight road and wants to reach position n$$$n$$$. Initially, she has 0$$$0$$$ stamina. On each day, she can do exactly one of the following:
Walk forward from position i$$$i$$$ to position i+1$$$i + 1$$$ and lose 1$$$1$$$ stamina. She can only do this if she has at least 1$$$1$$$ stamina.
Rest at her current position i$$$i$$$ and gain ai$$$a_i$$$ stamina.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains an integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤2⋅105$$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of positions on the road.
The second line of each test case contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,…,an$$$a_1, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤109$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the amount of stamina Alice gains by resting at position i$$$i$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, output one integer — the minimum number of days Alice needs to reach position n$$$n$$$.
note: In the first test case, Alice can rest at position 1$$$1$$$ for the first 3$$$3$$$ days and walk forward for the next 3$$$3$$$ days.
In the second test case, Alice can do the following:
Rest at position 1$$$1$$$. After this, her stamina is 1$$$1$$$.
Walk to position 2$$$2$$$. After this, her stamina is 0$$$0$$$.
Rest at position 2$$$2$$$. After this, her stamina is 2$$$2$$$.
Walk to position 3$$$3$$$. After this, her stamina is 1$$$1$$$.
Walk to position 4$$$4$$$. After this, her stamina is 0$$$0$$$.
